'''Sabine Ludwigs''' (born 1978) is a German chemist who is a full professor at the [[University of Stuttgart]]. Her research considers conductive molecular materials for technologies including organic electronics and actuators. She investigates the functional properties (optical, electronic, electrochemical) of conductive polymers.

== Early life and education ==
Ludwigs was born in [[Cologne]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Sabine Ludwigs {{!}} Expert {{!}} University of Stuttgart |url=https://www.uni-stuttgart.de/en/press/experts/Prof.-Sabine-Ludwigs/ |access-date=2024-04-14 |website=www.uni-stuttgart.de |language=en}}</ref> She was an undergraduate student at the [[University of Bayreuth]], where she remained for her doctoral research in physical chemistry.<ref name=":0" /> Her research involved investigations into the complex nanostructures that form in triblock terpolymer thin films.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Complex nanostructures in triblock terpolymer thin films {{!}} WorldCat.org |url=https://search.worldcat.org/title/836264880 |access-date=2024-04-14 |website=search.worldcat.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat. habil. Sabine Ludwigs {{!}} Institute of Polymer Chemistry {{!}} University of Stuttgart |url=https://www.ipoc.uni-stuttgart.de/fp/team/Ludwigs-00001/ |access-date=2024-04-14 |website=www.ipoc.uni-stuttgart.de |language=en}}</ref> She moved to the [[University of Cambridge]] as a postdoctoral researcher, where she spent two years.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Sabine Ludwigs — Freiburg Institute for Advanced Studies – FRIAS |url=https://www.frias.uni-freiburg.de/de/das-institut/archiv-frias/school-of-softmatter/fellows/ludwigs |access-date=2024-04-14 |website=www.frias.uni-freiburg.de |language=de}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 2006, Ludwigs established her own research group at the Institute for Macromolecular Chemistry at the [[University of Freiburg]].<ref name=":2" /> She was a Junior Fellow and awarded an [[Emmy Noether Fellowship]].<ref name=":1" /> She spent four years in the Freiburg Material Research Center before moving to the [[University of Stuttgart]] as Full Professor of Structure and Properties of Polymeric Materials.<ref name=":0" />

Ludwigs' research considers semiconducting molecular materials for next-generation technologies, including organic electronics and soft robotics. She investigates how molecular design impacts the functional properties of materials and structure-function relationships (e.g. how structure and morphology impacts optical and electronic properties). Alongside electrons, molecular materials can enable ionic transport, which makes them valuable materials for bioelectronics, personalised therapeutics and wearable medical devices.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |author=University of Stuttgart  |title=Autonomously switchable polymer materials developed for wearable medical devices |url=https://phys.org/news/2023-07-autonomously-switchable-polymer-materials-wearable.html |date=2023-07-18 |access-date=2024-04-14 |website=phys.org |language=en}}</ref>

Since 2020 she has served as Associate Editor of [[Macromolecules (journal)|Macromolecules]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2019-12-24 |editor-last=Hillmyer |editor-first=Marc A. |title=Editorial |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.macromol.9b02527 |journal=Macromolecules |language=en |volume=52 |issue=24 |pages=9425–9426 |doi=10.1021/acs.macromol.9b02527 |issn=0024-9297|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
